nom: Hypochlorous Acid Spray for Face and Skin; Facial Cleanser

segments.oily: The reviewer who describes her skin as acne-prone and oily reports less pigmented redness and fewer breakouts within the first two days of use.
segments.sensitive: Most reviewers with sensitive skin, including sensitive eyes and scent sensitivity, report the spray is gentle, fragrance-free and non-irritating; one reviewer cautions that this unbuffered formula's pH may drift over time, which could make it more irritating for sensitive or reactive skin such as rosacea or eczema.
segments.dry: The couple of reviewers who mention dry or itchy skin, including a persistently itchy patch that used to bleed from scratching, report the spray calmed the itching without worsening the dryness.

concerns.redness: Multiple reviewers report the spray reduces facial redness, describing it as soothing and less pigmented within days; no reviewer reports the spray increasing redness.
concerns.spots: One reviewer who applied the spray daily to a patch of eczema on her knee reports the area turned deep purple, then a dark pink, and remained discolored two weeks later even after she stopped use; the discoloration did not spread beyond the eczema patch itself.
concerns.blemishes: This is the most frequently reported benefit: many reviewers with acne-prone, cystic, hormonal, or teenage breakouts report fewer and milder breakouts within about a week; a minority instead report the spray broke them out, which one reviewer attributes to an unstabilized, overly chlorine-smelling batch.

extraits.texte: I was using a different brand that is more expensive and thought maybe I could try a more affordable spray. It smells like chlorine bad and broke my forehead out. I learned that HOCI will smell that way when it’s not stabilized, free chlorine. Glad it works for some but I will return and just stick to the one I’m used to with no smell or breakouts.

extraits.titre: It has many uses, but when I tried it on eczema on side of knee…the area turned it purple!
extraits.texte: This is a review for Hypochlorous Acid Spray for Face and Skin, Piercing Aftercare Spray, 8 oz Hypochlorous Acid Spray for Face, Skin, Acne, Eczema, Body Acne Sprays, Piercing Aftercare, Facial Wound Solution, Workout (8 Fl Oz (Pack of 1)) I’m not sure what to think of this product. It’s supposed to have many uses including healing eczema, so I thought I’d try it. I had a spot of eczema on the side of my knee. I used the spray four days in a row, just one pump of the spray then rubbed it into the side of my knee each morning. The evening of the fourth day, I noticed that the spot was a deep purple! I wasn’t and still am uncertain what to think of that. It was rather startling. I stopped using the spray and left the area alone. Two weeks later, while most, but not all of the eczema appears to be gone, the area is still discolored. It is no longer a deep purple, but is a dark shade of pink. It never itched or hurt, only discolored. I truly don’t know how to feel about this. I’m very glad I didn’t try this on my face as I’d rather not have purple or deep pink spots on my face! Now, having said this, the only area that changed color is the exact area that had the eczema. It didn’t bother my hands or the area surrounding the eczema, even though the Hypochlorous Acid was rubbed into those areas as well. Based on that, I don’t believe I’m allergic to it. extraits.titre: works quickly, wish spray was fine mist
extraits.texte: immediately noticed a difference within the first two days of using it! my redness isn’t as pigmented and I’ve been breaking out less (I have acne prone oily skin). only thing I don’t like about it is the spray nozzle, I wish it were more of a fine mist! Likely will transfer the liquid into another spray bottle.

Been using this for a week as a “toner” after I use my cleanser and omg what a difference it’s made! It smells kind of like peroxide which doesn’t bother me at all, it’s very gentle on the skin. Before this I was struggling with cystic acne breakouts out of no where. As a 40 Year old woman I was embarrassed and felt like a teenager again. I’m so happy I found this and happy with the results! I have not had a breakout in over a week!

extraits.titre: Buffering issue. I think it works but may not be ideal for sensitive skin
extraits.texte: I’ve purchased this spray a couple of time and have found it to be somewhat beneficial. Unlike some other reviews here, I actually weirdly like the slightly pool/chlorine smell. I have sprayed it just to get that blast of summer memories during the long winter months. It seems to calm down my acne and problematic skin, but I'm not sure how much. That being said, after doing more research, I realized I couldn’t find an official company website or clear brand information for “Aquia,” which made it difficult to verify how the product is formulated or tested. The ingredient list is very minimal (water + 0.015% hypochlorous acid), which suggests the formula may not be buffered. Btw, 0.015% HOCl = ~150 parts per million (ppm). That is within the typical skin-use range (100–200 ppm) Why does buffering matter? I did the deep dive so you don't have to, but please take note I'm just an ADHD mom on a mission and NOT a skin care professional. I guess hypochlorous acid tends to be most skin-friendly when its pH is kept stable. Without buffering, the chemistry can drift over time, which may increase the chlorine smell and be more irritating for people with sensitive or reactive skin (rosacea, eczema, etc). Ironically, the smell I enjoyed may actually be a sign of that instability. I didn’t know Hypochlorous Acid was a thing but it has definitely made a difference in my face. I tend to have redness in my face and when I use this spray it helps to reduce that. It’s sprays out fine. I don’t think it’s too thin or too thick. It goes on like any other spray bottle. I use it in the morning after cleansing my and toning my face. I let it sit on my skin and air dry. Once dry I can continue with my routine. It smells like nothing but water. The acid levels is under .02 percent so it’s not strong. If you are looking for a good Hypcholorous Acid this is a real contender.
